content:
The gray crescent in amphibian embryos contains determinants for dorsal structures and axis formation. When the first cleavage divides the embryo such that only one blastomere receives the gray crescent, that blastomere can develop into a complete (though smaller) embryo, while the blastomere without the gray crescent forms only a ventralized "belly piece" lacking proper organization.  

Final answer: (B)
